## [2026-10-31](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-31.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Compile Away Uncertainty: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Programmatic Compilation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39508>)

SkillCompiler turns well-specified operations within evolving agent skills into locally validated programs while retaining language-model reasoning for context-dependent decisions. A persistent program bank reuses compatible implementations across skills, reducing repeated procedural generation without updating model weights.

**Published:** 2026-10-29 · **First seen:** 2026-10-31T10:04:16.682+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agent Skills, Program Compilation, Execution Reliability

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39508v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections III–V and the operational appendix: across three independently learned banks, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reaches 98.26% success on 134 ALFWorld tasks, versus 93.53% for the strongest reported baseline. A separate fixed-bank LiveMath experiment repeats 100 tasks three times: mixed success/failure outcomes fall from SkillOpt’s 32% to 11%. Persistent banks are frozen before testing, although task-local program synthesis remains allowed. This is an unreported October 30 original-batch paper discovered in the lookback, not an October 31 release.

**Limitations:** Development included inspection of held-out failures. Local validation does not prove correctness for all inputs; evolution budgets differ and token/call savings are not uniform. No author code release was verified, and dynamic open-world robustness is unestablished.

## [2026-10-27](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-27.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35697>)

MiRL profiles recurring terminal-agent mistakes, resumes reinforcement-learning rollouts immediately before those mistakes, and rewards continuations only when tests pass and a behavior judge approves. This targeted practice reduces several measured misbehaviors and improves the tested compact agent while avoiding repeated generation of earlier task steps.

**Published:** 2026-10-26 · **First seen:** 2026-10-27T10:06:15.694+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agent Learning, Targeted RL, Terminal Agents

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35697v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/runchu-tian/MiRL>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–D inspect 219 reproducible prefixes from 189 environments, Qwen3.5-4B, and a judge checking five continuation steps. Three-run means are 51.8 versus 47.4 for TMax-4B on TB-Lite and 21.3 versus 20.6 on TB-2.1; 16-seed TB-2.1 means remain close. Newly-discovered editorial catch-up: the pinned October 25 repository already contains method/results before the October 26 paper receipt; exact historical public visibility is unproven, so no later paper-announcement timestamp is asserted as earliest work release.

**Limitations:** One backbone and one training run; checkpoint selection uses TB-Lite. Judge dependence and deterministic replay filtering constrain generality. Reported 35% rollout usage includes profiling but estimates the TMax denominator; it is not a measured universal compute saving. Code was inspected, not executed.

### [POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32448>)

POSEIDON turns executable scientific workflows into reproduction, subflow, completion and correction tasks, repairing rejected candidates through a generator–validator loop. The resulting Pearl collection improves the tested scientific agents, suggesting that extracting complementary tasks and broader repository coverage can make environment generation more useful.

**Published:** 2026-10-23 · **First seen:** 2026-10-26T10:04:55.008Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Training Environments, Scientific Agents, Synthetic Tasks

**Public availability:** 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32448v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The authors construct 97,659 environments from 7,110 repositories and train Qwen3.5 models on 64,477 successful teacher trajectories. The 27B model’s eight-column average rises from 44.3% to 51.5%; matched-size and task-removal ablations support diversity benefits. Three independent auditors approve 573 of 600 sampled environments. Original Monday cs.AI new-submission listing and schedule imply October26 00:00UTC announcement; the October23 receipt is retained.

**Limitations:** Repository selection deliberately favors biology; generated validators and reference solutions remain fallible. Evaluation filters tasks and mixes rule-based with model judging. ### [CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24960>)

CoworkEnv synthesizes coordinated service records, tool interfaces and executable graders, validates their consistency, and turns teacher executions into training demonstrations for compact work agents. SFT raises Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct's mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on 199 Claw-Eval tasks and improves a separate ClawMark-trained checkpoint from 11.8 to 19.4 on 100 tasks, showing how executable workflow construction can supply useful agent-training data.

**Published:** 2026-10-18 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.248Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Training Environments, Cowork Agents, Executable Grading

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24960>) · [Code](<https://github.com/HKUST-KnowComp/CoworkEnv>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Methods 3, Experiments 4, Limitations and Appendices A–F inspected. Capability plans generate requests, initial records, tools and weighted completion/prohibited-action checks; programmatic gates test parsing, service references, answer-identifier leakage and synthetic grading consistency, allowing one repair retry. Teacher-success and structure/length filters prepare assistant-token SFT; the mixed-pool replay retains937/1,809 demonstrations, while other export branches have distinct thresholds. Claw-Eval base/SFT comparisons use 161 General plus 38 Multi-turn tasks with three trials/task; the metric is mean fractional score on0–100, not binary success. The 77.8 versus 45.9 Multi-turn gain is 31.9 points. Separate ClawMark SFT is evaluated on 100tasks. Original cs.AI October 20 batch plus official schedule supports inferred paper availability2026-10-20T00:00Z; Sunday October 18 receipt is preserved. Observed initial GitHub pipeline contentOctober 19 at 20:36Z, lessons contentOctober 19 at 20:07Z and model uploadsOctober 19 at 17:57Z are in this same daily window; repository creation onOctober 16 alone is not evidence of earlier substantive availability. Classified conservatively as newly-discovered using the preserved October 18 receipt date within the 72-hour discovery window; earlier October 19 model/code content is acknowledged rather than using the later paper announcement as the earliest release of the work. This is editorial catch-up, not delayed indexing.

**Limitations:** Graders cover declared calls/records rather than all semantics: the documented ticket-update check does not verify resolution text. Teacher filtering can discard recovery behavior and favors a proprietary teacher. RL pipelines share supervised warm-up and vary multiple configuration choices, so their gains over the base cannot isolate RL or one credit-assignment mechanism. Public code is incremental: selected synthesis/adapters/SFT and RL-preprocessing components are present, while full distributed RL stack and task datasets are not bundled. Separate HF checkpoints are listed, but this review did not run or independently reproduce them.

## [2026-10-19](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-19.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22791>)

Self-HPO alternates failure-guided harness revisions with reinforcement learning of the coding policy, using the updated policy and its unsolved training tasks to guide the next search round. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, average resolve rate across three SWE benchmarks rises from 57.8% to 64.8%, offering a practical recipe for improving the model and its execution scaffold together rather than optimizing either component in isolation.

**Published:** 2026-10-16 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.248Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Learning, Harness Optimization, Coding Agents

**Public availability:** 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22791>) · [Code](<https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/Self-HPO>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Sections 2–3, Table 1–3 and relevant Appendices A–E inspected. Two rounds alternate six harness candidates with 50 GRPO/BAR updates on 2,484 Python engineering training tasks. The self-proposer sees training failures and reference fixes but must not inject reference patches into solving context. Main evaluation averages three runs on 500 SWE-Verified,300 SWE-Multilingual and642 public V2 SWE-Pro tasks. Self-HPO scores 69.5/59.7/65.2 versus 61.0/54.2/58.3 for Base and 67.5/56.3/61.8 for matched policy-only RLVR. Cross-combinations retain some gains separately, with the final pair 69.5 exceeding 64.5 from evolved harness/base policy and 64.4 from seed harness/final policy. Original cs.CL October 19 batch plus official Eastern announcement schedule supports inferred paper availability2026-10-19T00:00Z; October 16 receipt is preserved. GitHub initial content commitOctober 19 at 01:39Z and HF model sole initial-release commitOctober 19 at 01:41Z corroborate the same window; earlier empty destination creation dates do not establish an earlier method release.

**Limitations:** Only one backbone and coding domain; harness and policy receive different optimization operations, so the comparison does not establish universal compute-normalized superiority. Training uses executable reference outcomes and proposer-accessible training fixes, and policy training required eight B200 GPUs. Three-run means do not prove general deployment reliability; no independent reproduction. External-proposer HPO 71.6 is a separate Opus 4.8 setting and is not attributed to Self-HPO.

### [Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22174>)

Mosaic trains agents across context-compaction and subagent sessions by combining outcome-aware session-use guidance with a per-session signal based on changes in correct-answer likelihood. This assigns more specific feedback to useful state transfers, improving BrowseComp success while reducing average session counts in the tested 4B agent.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:07:30.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Learning, Context Compaction, Credit Assignment, Subagents

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?show=1000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22174>) · [Project](<https://lark-ai-lab.github.io/Mosaic/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Methods 3.1–3.2, Table 1 and Appendices C–D specify critic-free shaping, type-wise normalization and matched training. With Qwen3.5-4B, compaction accuracy rises 35.31→38.86% while sessions fall 3.17→2.35; forking rises 31.44→32.46% with 4.43→3.77 sessions. Training uses 1,000 REDSearcher tasks; BrowseComp evaluation covers 1,266 questions. ArXiv availability is inferred from its original dated batch and official schedule.

**Limitations:** One backbone and benchmark; session count is a proxy rather than measured end-to-end cost. Correct answers are needed for training-time likelihood scoring, and immediate gains approximate branching-session contributions. Production asynchrony is untested. The project was retrieved, but no released implementation was verified. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-14](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-14.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18484>)

ReTerm teaches terminal agents to recover from their own failed environment states, first using teacher-generated repair demonstrations and then mixing ordinary and recovery rollouts during reinforcement learning. Its bounded queue of recent failure states keeps recovery practice aligned with the evolving policy; the authors' matched 9B-model evaluation improves Terminal-Bench 2.0 from 20.2% to 34.8% Pass@1.

Sections 3–4 describe pre-verifier VM snapshots, teacher-only SFT loss and separate group normalization for original/recovery tasks. Table 4 reports 25.8% for recovery SFT, 28.0% for standard GRPO and 34.8% for ReTerm-GRPO. Nautil trains investigators to gather evidence, track competing explanations, and decide whether a case supports a conclusion or should remain open. ## [2026-10-03](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-03.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01787>)

Component Routing divides a GUI agent's experience into interface locations, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then chooses whether each belongs in model weights or retrieved context. A rule based on recurrence and dependence on the current state offers a practical way to combine fine-tuning with memory instead of sending every experience through the same route.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:36:41.826Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** GUI Agents, Experience Reuse, Memory

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.01787v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Paired held-out tests span three 7–8B model families, MobileGym and AndroidWorld, and three seeds, with deterministic task checkers. Routing improves over the better single destination by 3.5 percentage points on average. Inspected but deferred in the Oct 2 run; first inclusion uses newly-discovered because its Oct 2 public release is within this report's lookback and it has never been published here.

**Limitations:** The route rule is calibrated on a narrow set of GUI models and extracted components, with structured-state or accessibility matching. Some component contrasts include zero, and routing does not beat the best single destination in every configuration. Code and data are described as a future release; no independent reproduction.
